fields.name: Lumen
fields.description: A photo catalogue that reads exposure data and sorts a shoot into keepers, maybes and rejects.

fields.audience: Photographers returning from a shoot with a thousand frames
fields.problem: Culling by eye takes longer than the shoot did, and tired eyes get inconsistent.
fields.goal: Cut the first pass of a cull from hours to minutes without hiding good frames.

fields.ownership: Wrote the scoring, the catalogue format and the viewer.

fields.approach: Score every frame for sharpness, blink, exposure and duplicates, then show a ranked contact sheet.
fields.tools: Python, OpenCV, SQLite, a small web viewer.
fields.decisions:
Never delete. Lumen only proposes, so a wrong call costs a click, not a photograph.
A sidecar file per image keeps the catalogue portable.

fields.challenge: Sharpness scores fooled by intentional motion blur and shallow focus.
fields.solution: Score the subject region, found by face and saliency, instead of the whole frame.
fields.tradeoff: Slower per image, but far fewer wrongly rejected keepers.

fields.result: A 1,200-frame wedding shoot sorted in under four minutes on a laptop.
fields.evidence: Compared against a manual cull of the same shoot: 94% of manual keepers landed in the top group.
fields.limitations: One photographer, one genre. Sports and low light are untested.

fields.learned: Showing why a frame scored low is worth more than the score.
fields.next_steps: Learn from my own keep and reject choices.
